current_date: 1 July 2019 (the list applies to applications submitted on or after 1 July 2019)
current_evidence: The council's 'Submit a Planning Application Online' page still says the National and Local List of Validation requirements applies to all applications submitted on or after 1 July 2019. A site-restricted search of basildon.gov.uk found no newer list.

issues.detail: Grokbot captured only about 15 items and missed many local requirements in the 2019 list: Biodiversity Survey and Report (where protected or priority species, SSSI/Local Wildlife Sites or priority habitats may be affected); Health Impact Assessment (all EIA-qualifying development); Heritage Statement (Listed Building Consent and applications affecting designated or non-designated heritage assets or Local Value Register buildings); Land Contamination Assessment (major or brownfield, EIA, or known contamination; Grokbot has only the guidance-booklet sentence); Lighting Assessment (external flood lighting, all applications except householder); Noise Assessment (major residential affected by road, rail or industrial noise; B2/B8 or late-night A3-A5 uses next to homes); Parking and Access Arrangements (any loss or gain of parking); Town Centre Impact Assessment (retail or leisure over 2,500 sq m, or main town centre uses out of centre); Statement of Community Involvement (large-scale or controversial schemes); Telecommunications supporting information (ICNIRP declaration, area of search); Transport Assessment (majors or a material increase in traffic on a trunk road).
issues.evidence: Local List July 2019 entries: Biodiversity Survey and Report, Health Impact Assessment, Heritage Statement, Lighting Assessment, Noise Assessment, Parking and Access, Town Centre Impact Assessment, SCI, Telecommunications, Transport Assessment

issues.detail: Ventilation / Extraction details is placed under Householder, but the source applies it to A3/A4/A5 uses and other proposals 'except householders'. Grokbot's own excerpt contains that exclusion.
issues.evidence: 'A3, A4 and A5 uses and any other proposals (except householders) which will incorporate a ventilation/extraction system'

issues.detail: The Householder 'Schedule of works (listed building)' row has an unrelated excerpt (Arboricultural Method Statement plus ventilation text). The 2019 local list has no schedule-of-works requirement for householder applications, so the row is spurious.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt: 'o Arboricultural Method Statement (if development is taking place within the root protection area) Ventilation/ Extraction System A3, A4 and A5 uses...'

issues.detail: Several triggers are fragments that do not state the threshold. Drainage/SuDS ('the proposed sustainable drainage system, in line with Paragraphs 103 and 109...') should be major development: 10+ dwellings, >0.5 ha, >1,000 sq m or 1 ha+. Flood Risk Assessment quotes FRA content instead of the trigger: Flood Zone 2/3, or Flood Zone 1 over 1 ha. EIA ('would constitute EIA development.') is a fragment. Tree survey ('include an Arboricultural Statement...') omits the trigger: trees on or next to the site, TPO or Conservation Area trees. Travel Plan states the content, not the trigger: significant transport generation.
issues.evidence: Local List: FRA 'Flood Zone 2 or 3; or Flood Zone 1 sites over 1 ha'; SuDS '10+ dwellings ... 1 ha or more'

issues.detail: Affordable Housing Statement and Viability Assessment are listed as separate rows with the same excerpt. In the source they are a single item, 'Affordable Housing Statement / Viability Statement' (10+ units or >0.2 ha; viability appraisal if below 36% affordable). Planning Obligations / S106 repeats the same 36% affordable text.
issues.evidence: 'Affordable Housing Statement / Viability Statement Application for new residential development where Sites of 10 units or more, or Sites of more than 0.2 Hectares'

issues.detail: All Full planning rows are marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. Outline gets only national drawing items (block plan, elevations), and Discharge of conditions gets a Block Plan row that is a national 'All' drawing requirement, not a local one. Local items such as Affordable Housing, FRA, SuDS (which has a separate outline checklist), Transport Assessment and Biodiversity apply equally to Outline. Listed Building Consent is shown as '(none)' although the Heritage Statement explicitly applies to it, and prior approval is '(none)' although telecoms prior approvals need the telecoms information.
issues.evidence: Heritage Statement: 'Listed Building Consent'; SuDS: 'Separate checklists exist for full and outline applications'; Telecommunications: 'Prior approval and planning applications for telecoms'

issues.detail: Both tab_items are process or advice text, not requirements: 'For applications submitted as a paper copy, 2 complete sets of documents must be submitted' and the advice to follow the 'Land Affected by Contamination' booklet.

The list is over 7 years old and predates statutory Biodiversity Net Gain (Feb 2024). The council has a separate BNG page but has not updated its local list. Users should be warned that the list is old and that national requirements such as BNG apply in addition.
issues.evidence: basildon.gov.uk/article/9941/Biodiversity-Net-Gain-BNG exists separately; the local list is dated 1 July 2019

summary: Grokbot's link is still Basildon's current local list (1 July 2019), but the extraction is thin. It misses about 11 local requirements (biodiversity, heritage, noise, lighting, transport assessment, town centre impact and others), puts ventilation under Householder despite the source's explicit exclusion, and has fragmentary triggers.
